newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hartley Poynton Q1 profit soars.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hartley Poynton Q1 profit soars.

text.p: Perth-based stockbroker, Hartley Poynton Ltd said on Tuesday its pre-tax profit for the three months to September 30 rose 57 percent to A$1.8 million compared to the previous corresponding quarter.
"The directors are pleased to note that this quarterley profit result was achieved with no contributions from any significant corporate transactions," the company said.

Hartley Poynton listed on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) on August 5 this year after a A$10 million capital raising. The company reported an after tax profit of A$5.6 million in the year to June 30 on revenue of A$36.4 million.

"Whilst appreciating that the nature of our business is cyclical, we are committed to the process of securing improved quality of earnings and achieving further growth in our existing broking, funds management and investment management businesses," Hartley Poynton's chairman, Jack Clough told the company's annual meeting in Perth.
Clough said the company's most important asset was people.
"Amongst our 131 staff we now have more depth of expertise and breadth of experience than ever before," he said. "The team's enthusiasm and focus is matched by their unity of purpose."
Over 60 percent of Hartley Poynton's capital is owned by staff and every employee is a shareholder which reinforced core values that employees think and act like owners, Clough said.
Hartley Poynton shares last traded at 96 cents on Monday.
